request: What did CRS report about Medicare prescription drug price negotiation and its expected savings?

reply.reply: CRS reported that CBO forecast Medicare’s drug-price negotiation program would reduce federal Medicare drug spending by $25 billion in 2031. CBO also projected average negotiated-drug net prices would be about 50% lower, with average Part D net prices 9% lower and Part B prices 8% lower in 2031 (CRS R47872, PDF p. 15). These are forecasts, not realized savings. The estimate is from CRS’s December 2023 report; the newer infographic’s text could not be verified. See the [brief](output/briefs/case-20261025-153541-5939.html).
reply.reasoning: The verified CRS quote directly states the CBO savings and price projections. Clearly label as forecasts, and note that reviewed text was from 2023.
